briefing.situationSummary: No single shock dominated the month, but the staff burden did shape what became credible.
briefing.riskPosture: The headquarters is now carrying more decision weight than at least one directorate can cleanly execute.
briefing.commandersIntent: Preserve the gain in credible readiness without letting the staff outrun itself.
briefing.operationalPicture: The force held the line and kept credible readiness from slipping backward.
briefing.decisionFocus: Reduce staff overload before asking for another visible move.
openQuestions: Which assumption in this month’s brief is most likely to fail next?
What did the room ask of sustainment that it has not yet actually earned?
Where is the next political cost likely to surface first?

campaignObjectives.label: Reach 7 or more deployable brigades
campaignObjectives.note: A posture only deters if the force behind it can actually deploy — looking active is not the same as being usable.

campaignObjectives.label: Keep alliance political alignment at 56 or more
campaignObjectives.note: Partners are watching for consistency. If reassurance drifts while you are still rebuilding, the coalition starts hedging on its own.

campaignObjectives.label: Keep cabinet cover at 32 or more
campaignObjectives.note: Cabinet cover is what lets you spend political capital on hard choices. Once it collapses, the theater plan stops being implementable, whatever the force can still do.

campaignObjectives.label: Keep the incident ladder at 58 or lower
campaignObjectives.note: Every visible move carries some escalation risk. The force has to rebuild a credible posture without stumbling into a crisis spiral it did not choose.

briefing.geopoliticalSummary: Pressure is rising, but the picture still favors a controlled recovery if the headquarters keeps its line of effort tight.

staffFunctions.label: Personnel
staffFunctions.standingRemit: Protects how many brigades you can field, whether retention holds, and how much recovery debt the force is quietly building up.

afterAction.heading: What changed this month
afterAction.detail: Deployable force shifted +1.35 brigades; cabinet cover shifted +0.4; incident ladder shifted +2.9.

afterAction.heading: What the headquarters underestimated
afterAction.detail: You asked more of Intelligence than it could absorb cleanly, so this followed: lower confidence and contradictory briefing.

afterAction.heading: Where your staff stand now
afterAction.detail: S1 recovery debt is 34, S2 visibility is estimated, S3 credible deterrence is 46.53 (visible 51 / executable 53.47), S4 supportable tempo is 2.88, and S5 strategic coherence is 57.6.

afterAction.heading: S4 support warning
afterAction.detail: Supportable tempo is 2.88. What logistics can actually support is now the hard limit on any further activity this month, whatever else the plan says.

afterAction.heading: Doctrine: unacknowledged risk
afterAction.detail: 4 staff lanes were strained or overloaded this month and none of it was explicitly accepted going in. An under-resourced lane can still surprise you even when the headline numbers look fine.

afterAction.heading: Doctrine: system pressure
afterAction.detail: The contested information picture (system pressure 69.18) is thin enough that mis-targeting or dependency blowback is a live risk this month.

afterAction.heading: Doctrine: underpriced-lane dissent
afterAction.detail: The staff underprices Training; it went under-resourced this month and surfaced as staff dissent rather than a clean warning.

afterAction.heading: Doctrine: neglected priority lane
afterAction.detail: The staff's natural priority (Sustainment) was left light while Intelligence ran overloaded.

summary: Standing at month 2: 6.5 brigades deployable, alliance alignment 52, cabinet cover 51, incident ladder 37.
